rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden owner harvested enough for his family, gave surplus to the needy, and allowed gleaners to collect missed grain and grapes.
rows.anchor: ويتصدق بالباقي على المحتاجين، ويترا ما يخطئه المنجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His sons resented this generosity and, after his death, resolved to gather the crop secretly and leave nothing for anyone in need.
rows.anchor: وكان بنوه يضيقون بذلك ويحاولون حمله على بما يملك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One report identifies the visitor who destroyed the garden as Satan; another identifies him as Gabriel, who uprooted and transported the trees around the Kaaba before planting them at Taif.
rows.anchor: طاف طائف - قيل في رواية إنه الشيطان، وفي أخرى إنه جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While the owners slept, the garden was made barren; in the morning they found it harvested, recognized their loss, and the middle brother reminded them of their neglect of God and His bounty.
rows.anchor: وترك الجنة صريماً جرداء خلاء. فلما أصبحوا، تنادوا ليغدوا على حرثهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The early Meccan account omits personal names, dates, and other details except where they serve its lesson; it identifies the people only as from Ethiopia or Yemen.
rows.anchor: لا يتعلق فيها بذكر الأشخاص والأزمنه إلا ما كان من جوهر القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran leaves the story's date unstated and gives no basis for the strange claims that Satan or Gabriel uprooted the trees and carried them to the Kaaba and Taif.
rows.anchor: دون أن يشير من قرب أو بعد، إلى ما يسيغ الروايات الغريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus 10:24 offers a useful parallel for understanding the garden story as a picture of worldly life suddenly cut down.
rows.anchor: لأن نستأنس في فهم آيات القلم، بآية يونس في مثل الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun in we tested them refers to the deniers and every oath-breaking, contemptible person.
rows.anchor: عائد على المكذبين وكل حلاف مهين

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: One interpretation compares Quraysh's trial to the garden owners' punishment by citing the seven-year famine, when Quraysh ate hides.
rows.anchor: قول من قالوا: النازل بقريش المماثل لأمر الجنة، هو الجدب

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Another interpretation compares the garden owners' planned deprivation of the poor with Quraysh's vow before Badr to kill the Prophet and his companions, followed by their defeat.
rows.anchor: تشبيه بلاء قريش ببلاء أصحاب الجنة، هو أن أهل الجنة عزموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Badr interpretation reads later history into the passage, since Badr occurred about five years after this surah; the warning addresses tyrants generally.
rows.anchor: النص، على أي حال، صريح في ردع كل الطغاة المتجبرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment verse points to the lesson of the garden story: tyrants face punishment in this world, while the hereafter's punishment is greater.
rows.anchor: يلفت إلى مناط العبرة فيما تلت الآيات من أمر أصحاب الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in if they knew refers to the tyrannical deniers tested by the story, rather than the garden owners who admitted wrongdoing, repented, and turned to God.
rows.anchor: من الطغاة المكذبين الذين نزلت القصة عبرة لهم ومثلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative does not disclose the garden owners' eventual fate, leaving it to God's knowledge and mercy, then turns its warning toward the opponents of the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أمسك عن ذكر مصيرهم، فأمرهم متروك إلى علم الله ورحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions reject and ridicule Quraysh's assumption that God would treat Muslims like criminals, affirming the different outcomes of the righteous and the sinful.
rows.anchor: إلى الرفض والإنكار: أن يجعل الله المسلمين كالمجرمين

none: The segment contains only the complete surah text.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah al-Asr is an early Meccan surah, conventionally ranked thirteenth in revelation, after al-Sharh and before al-Adiyat.
rows.anchor: السورة مكية مبكرة، والمشهور في ترتيبها أنها الثالثة عشرة في النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of asr is pressing to extract juice, as in squeezing grapes; related words name the press, place of pressing, and stones used for it.
rows.anchor: والمعنى الأصلي للعصر لغة: الضغط لاستخلاص العصارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic also calls rain-bearing clouds mu'sirat, says a people asaru when they bring rain, and uses i'sar for a strong wind driving clouds.
rows.anchor: وسميت السحب الممطرة معصرات لما تعتصر من المطر، وأعصر القوم أمطروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic also uses asr metaphorically for confinement and extraction by pressure, and derives words for age and lineage from the image of pressing out an essence.
rows.anchor: ومن هذه الدلالة اللغوية الأصلية على الضغط والإعتصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The age is called asr because experience and hardship press out a person's essence; late afternoon is also asr as the day is brought to its close, and the prayer takes its name from that time.
rows.anchor: سمي الدهر عصراً، بملحظ من استخلاصه عصارة الإنسان بالضغط والتجربة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic uses of the root include squeezing grapes in Yusuf 12:36 and rain clouds in al-Naba 78:14, alongside the verb in Yusuf 12:49.
rows.anchor: بمعناه اللغوي الأول في اعتصار الخمر بآية يوسف 36

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root also appears for a whirlwind in al-Baqara 2:266 and for asr in the surah itself.
rows.anchor: والإعصار في آية البقرة 266. والعصر، في سورة العصر

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Among the meanings of the oath, al-Tabari reports both the age and a particular time of day, then prefers the age.
rows.anchor: في تفسيره، ثم اختار الدهر

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi lists the afternoon prayer, understood with an omitted noun, and the age of Prophethood among the proposed meanings, without an explicit preference.
rows.anchor: وقيل أنه صلاة العصر، على حذف المضاف، أو هو عصر النبوة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari appears to prefer the afternoon prayer because of its merit and difficulty during the busy end of the workday; he cites the report comparing a missed prayer to losing one's family and property.
rows.anchor: ولأن التكليف في أدائها أشق لتهافت الناس في تجارتهم ومكاسبهم آخر النهار

rows.speaker: محمد عبده
rows.claim: Muhammad Abdu says Arabs gathered at afternoon to talk, so the oath corrects the belief that time itself is blameworthy when harmful conduct may occur then.
rows.anchor: وكان من عادة العرب أن يجتمعوا وقت العصر، ويتحادثوا ويتذكروا

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: Ibn Qayyim prefers reading asr as the age, as do most exegetes.
rows.anchor: الراجح عند "ابن قيم الجوزية" أنه الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's waw retains its basic linguistic force of magnifying what is sworn by; al-Tabari did not construct elaborate arguments for the greatness of asr.
rows.anchor: والسورة تبدأ بواو القسم وهو عندهم على أصل استعماله اللغوي

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi assembles six reasons for the greatness of the age, three for a particular time of day, six for the afternoon prayer, and a further case for the Prophetic age.
rows.anchor: جمع الرازي ستة وجوه في عظمة العصر بمعنى الدهر

rows.speaker: محمد عبده
rows.claim: The author rejects Muhammad Abdu's claim that afternoon was the customary time for gatherings: evening may fit better, and objectionable talk is possible at any time.
rows.anchor: ولا نعلم أن هذا الوقت في المألوف والعادة وقت اجتماع الناس وتذاكرهم

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi's reasons for magnifying the age include its extraordinary changes, the value of the final moment of life, and time's rank over space.
rows.anchor: ولا تكاد أقوالهم تخرج عما استوفاه الفخر الرازي من وجوه عظمة العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author follows al-Tabari, Ibn Qayyim, and most exegetes in reading asr as the age, and confines discussion to the arguments offered for that meaning.
rows.anchor: ومن حيث آثرنا مع الطبري وابن القيم، وأكثر المفسرين، أن يكون العصر بمعنى الدهر

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi calls time a wonder encompassing fortune and hardship, health and illness, and wealth and poverty, while resisting simple judgments that it either exists or does not.
rows.anchor: فعلمت حينئذ أن أشرف الأشياء حياتك في هذه اللمحة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says even a final instant can secure eternal paradise after a wasted lifetime, making time one of the greatest blessings.
rows.anchor: إن بقية عمر المرء لا قيمة لها، فلو ضيعت ألف سنة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi regards time as nobler than space and says the oath answers people who blame the age for calamities: the fault lies in the human being, not time.
rows.anchor: إن الزمان أعلى وأشرف من المكان، فكان القسم بالعصر قسماً بأشرف النصفين

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says passing time subtracts from one's lifespan; without a corresponding gain, that decrease is itself loss, even when people welcome time passing.
rows.anchor: ذكر العصر الذي بمضيه ينتقص عمرك، فإذا لم يكن في مقابلته كسب

rows.speaker: ابن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn Qayyim sees the ordered alternation of night and day, their changing light and temperature, and time divisions as signs of God's power and wisdom; the oath links human actions in time to their judgment.
rows.anchor: فأقسم بالعصر الذي هو زمان أفعال الإنسان ومحلها، على عاقبة تلك الأفعال وجزائها

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi compares evening to the world's destruction and morning to resurrection, urging people to use their remaining lifespan for a trade without loss.
rows.anchor: أن آخر النهار يشبه تخريب العالم وإماتة الأحياء كما أن أول النهار يشبه بعث الأموات

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi says the world's remaining life is like the time between afternoon and sunset, so people should hasten a trade without loss.
rows.anchor: الدنيا ما بقى إلا بقدر ما بين العصر إلى المغرب، فعلى الإنسان أن يشتغل بتجارة لا خسران فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the prophetic report against blaming time, since God is al-dahr.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: لا تسبوا الدهر فإن الله هو الدهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report describes time as strangely both existent and like nothing, and compares a person's lifetime to a small part of it.
rows.anchor: من أعجايب الدهر الدالة على كمال قدره خالقها: أن الدهر موجود يشبه المعدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects loading asr with philosophical and mystical interpretations; the Quran explains signs of night and day in accessible terms, as in al-Qasas 28:71-72.
rows.anchor: وترى أنهم حملوا لفظ العصر كل هذه التأويلات الفلسفية والإشارية مما

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi suggests the Quran chose asr instead of dahr because unbelievers were fond of invoking and exalting the latter word.
rows.anchor: ولعله تعالى لم يذكر الدهر لعلمه أن الملحد مولع بذكره وتعظيمه

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nisaburi explains the oath as honoring the age and cites the report that people should not curse time because God is al-dahr.
rows.anchor: على حين يذهب النيسابورى إلى أن وجه الإقسام بالعصر هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads asr as the age that presses and tests humanity, extracting its essence; this familiar Arabic sense leads into the declaration that humanity is in loss.
rows.anchor: تأتي كلمة العصر في سياقها من السورة، لافتة إلى ابتلاء الإنسان بالعصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's waw moves from a perceptible reality to a moral truth, a pattern the author also discusses in other surahs.
rows.anchor: الواو هنا في موضعها الذي تطرد به الظاهرة الأسلوبية في اللفت إلى حسى مدرك

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes differ between taking the human as all people and as particular Meccan opponents; reports name al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Lahab, or Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: مراداً بالإنسان جماعة من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that the exception of believers would break if humanity meant only the named Meccan opponents.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستثناء ينقطع إذا ما كان الإنسان خاصاً بالمعهودين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects restricting humanity to named disbelievers: the general wording and the exception for believers would not fit people who never became believers.
rows.anchor: ولا نقف عندما اختلفوا فيه، فالعبرة بعموم اللفظ لا بخصوص السبب

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari understands humanity as a collective plural; al-Zamakhshari calls it the species generally, Abu Hayyan a generic noun, and Ibn Qayyim likely agrees.
rows.anchor: الإنسان بمعنى الجمع لا بمعنى الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's use of al-nas denotes humanity broadly, while al-ins appears in contexts paired with jinn and carries the sense of human beings as the opposite of wild creatures.
rows.anchor: فشهد ذلك بأن دلالة الإنسية، بما تعني من نقيض الوحشية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah al-Asr and al-Balad establish social responsibility, especially enjoining right and forbidding wrong, as a foundation of religion and a means of avoiding loss.
rows.anchor: فبمثل هذا التقرير الحاسم في سورتى العصر والبلد، تتقرر مسئولية الإنسان الاجتماعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran condemns Israelites who failed to forbid wrongdoing and hypocrites who commanded evil and withheld good.
rows.anchor: كانوا لا يتناهون عن منكر فعلوه لبئس ما كانوا يفعلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author argues that no secular law can raise people to Islam's level of social responsibility, which grounds goodness and faith and protects from ruin.
rows.anchor: هيهات لشريعة وضعية أن ترقى بالإنسان إلى مثل هذا المستوى

none: The segment contains only the surah text and no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah al-Layl is conventionally ninth in revelation, after al-Ala and before al-Fajr and al-Duha; although it follows al-Shams in the codex, al-Shams was revealed later.
rows.anchor: أنها تاسعة السور، نزلت بعد سورة الأعلى، ثم نزلت بعدها

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Some connect al-Layl with al-Shams in the codex: after the outcomes of purification and corruption, this surah identifies the actions that bring success or failure and who enters or avoids the Fire.
rows.anchor: وهذا الربط قديلفت إلى ملحظ في ترتيب السورة في المصحف

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Reports say the surah concerned Abu Bakr's spending and Umayya ibn Khalaf's stinginess; another account concerns Abu al-Dahdah buying a palm tree after a hypocrite or Jew refused the Prophet's offer of a tree in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وفي قول آخر إنها نزلت في أبي الدحداح الأنصاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever its occasion, the lesson is universal because the passage directly addresses people generally: their efforts differ.
rows.anchor: والعبرة على كل حال بعموم اللفظ، والسياق صريح التوجيه إلى عامة الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearby revelations of al-Layl, al-Fajr, and al-Duha develop a Quranic image pattern using gradations of light and darkness for guidance and misguidance.
rows.anchor: يجلو الظاهرة الأسلوبية التي يعمد فيها البيان القرآني إلى جلاء المعنويات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root gh-sh-y means covering; its derivatives describe a veil, dulling of perception in sleep or fainting, and the covering of sight or insight.
rows.anchor: ومن غشية النعاس المعطلة للحس والإدراك، جاءت غشية الإغماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran uses covering for rejection in Noah 71:7 and Hud 11:5, for the overwhelming manifestation at the lote tree, and for sleep, fainting, or a veil over heart and senses.
rows.anchor: وفي الاستعمال القرآني، جاءت الغاشية على معناها في استغشاء الثياب حاجزاً دون السمع والبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root often describes the Day of Judgment and its punishments covering people, faces, or places.
rows.anchor: وكثر مجئ الغشية في الحديث عن يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root can name terrors or darkness; the author understands night in this surah as a covering of deep darkness.
rows.anchor: والغواشي الأهوال، أو الظلمات تلقى لفاعها الأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word tajalli means appearing or becoming uncovered; its physical senses include recession of the hairline, polish that clears sight, display of a bride, and polishing a blade or mirror.
rows.anchor: والتجلي لغة الظهور والإنكشاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran uses the root for exile from the land in al-Hashr 59:3, divine manifestation to the mountain in al-Araf 7:143, and the Hour being made manifest in 7:187.
rows.anchor: في خمية مواضع، إحداها آية الحشر في الجلاء عن الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining uses concern the illumination of day in al-Shams and al-Layl.
rows.anchor: والمرات الأربع الباقية في تجلي النور الإلهي بآية الأعراف 143

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes supply an unstated object for the night covering: the whole day, the sun, or the earth and everything in it; they likewise explain daylight's appearing as the removal of night or the sun's light.
rows.anchor: أو يغشى الشمس، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees no deleted or implied object; the night covering and day appearing are themselves the intended focus, so no object needs to be named.
rows.anchor: يصرفنا عن تأويل محذوف أو مقدر، لنلتفت إلى أن الغشية والتجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes treat the oath's waw as magnifying night and day, but the author allows that a rhetorical device can depart from its original grammatical use, as interrogatives and commands do.
rows.anchor: قد يعدل عن هذا الأصل لملحظ بلاغي في التعبير، كمثل عدوله في الاستفهام

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God swore by night and day because of their great importance as two signs that God turns over creation.
rows.anchor: لعظم شأنهما، فهما آيتان عظيمتان يكورهما الله على الخلائق

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan explains the oath through the roles of night as the time creatures shelter and day as the time they spread out.
rows.anchor: أقسم بالليل الذي فيه كل حيوان يأوى إلى مأواه

rows.speaker: ابن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn Qayyim says God swears by night in all its states because it is one of His signs.
rows.anchor: إذ هو من آياته الدالة عليه

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi details how night brings shelter, sleep, and rest while daylight reveals the world and enables work; their alternation serves human needs.
rows.anchor: فلو كان الدهر كله ليلاً لتعذر المعاش، ولو كان نهاراً كله لبطلت الراحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the general usefulness of alternating night and day is not the specific point of this oath; the Quran explains those benefits directly elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وهذا الكلام في المصلحة من تعاقب الليل والنهار، هو من قبيل الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran explains the practical wisdom of day and night directly, for example by contrasting endless night and day in al-Qasas 28:71-72.
rows.anchor: والقرآن حين يقصد إلى أن يلفت إلى آيتي الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author contrasts this oath's specific conditions of night and day with the many Quranic statements that explain their benefits and changing states.
rows.anchor: بغير غشية الليل وتجلي النهار، نلمح السر البياني

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes read ma in the oath either as man, meaning the Creator of male and female, or as a verbal noun meaning the creation of male and female.
rows.anchor: فيكون القسم بمن خلق الذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes cite a poetic line where a genitive form is explained as standing for a verbal noun; the author considers grammatical proximity more likely and says the comparison is inexact because the verse has ma while the poem does not.
rows.anchor: والجر هنا أقرب عندي إلى أن يحمل على المجاورة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi and Abu Hayyan report that male and female mean Adam and Eve, all human males and females, or male and female members of every animal kind.
rows.anchor: ففي تفسير الرازي والبحر المحيط، أنهما آدم وحواء، أو هما كل ذكر

rows.speaker: ابن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn Qayyim connects the pairings: night and day arise through celestial bodies, while male and female arise among earthly bodies; both are signs of God's lordship.
rows.anchor: فإن إخراج الليل والنهار بواسطة الأجرتم العلوية

rows.speaker: ابن القيم
rows.claim: Ibn Qayyim also links time and the human actors within it to differing actions and rewards, comparing that difference to the contrasting pairs in the oath.
rows.anchor: على اختلاف السعي كما اختلف الليل والنهار والذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author centers the surah's pattern of contrasts: visible differences between night and day and male and female prepare for differences in people's actions and their recompense.
rows.anchor: ما يسيطر على السورة كلها من ملحظ التقابل والتفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sa'y literally means walking but implies purposeful work pursued with effort and persistence.
rows.anchor: فكان السعي بمعنى العمل مع القصد والدأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quranic sa'y can denote literal or figurative movement, as with Moses's staff, the magicians' illusion, and believers' light on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: نجد الدلالة الأولى للسعي بمعنى المشي والحركة، على الحقيقة أو التخييل والمجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sa'y also means sustained work in pursuit of an aim, as in the passages about accepted deeds, seeking the afterlife, and people whose efforts go astray.
rows.anchor: كما نجد دلالة السعي على العمل مع الدأب في آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other uses make the directed purpose especially clear, such as striving to ruin mosques or spreading corruption on earth.
rows.anchor: وواضح أن السعي في آية الليل، هو من العمل الكسبي مع القصد والدأب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatta derives from separation and difference; ashtatan denotes scattering, while shatta denotes divergence or variation, which the next verses explain without further interpretation.
rows.anchor: أما شتى، فمن الاختلاف والتباين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrasts between giving and withholding explain the divergent human efforts that the earlier images of night and day and male and female prepared for.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو تفاوت السعي، يأتي بعد أن مهد له اللفت إلى التفاوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Husn means beauty and is used materially against ugliness and morally against evil; husna is a feminine superlative for the utmost good, opposed to saw'a.
rows.anchor: والحسن في اللغة الجمال، ويغلب استعماله في الماديات

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes husn, used for objects and events, hasana, which as a noun is used for events, and husna, used only for events.
rows.anchor: وفرق الراغب فب (المفردات) بين الحسن والحسنة والحسنى

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes interpret al-husna as a good outcome, belief in God's oneness, or confidence that God will repay the spender; the author says good outcome can encompass all three.
rows.anchor: وقد تأول المفسرون الحسنى بحسن العاقبة، وبالإيمان بوحدانية الله

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: The author follows Abu Hayyan that the omitted objects of giving leave the recipient and gift unspecified, praising generosity whether obligatory, voluntary, or gracious.
rows.anchor: بأن المقصود الثناء على المعطى دون تعرض للمعطى والعطية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's uses of stinginess concern wealth and God's bounty; giving in this contrast therefore concerns spending from wealth.
rows.anchor: وكل بخل في القرآن يتعلق بالمال وبما آتى الله من فضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast concerns giving away wealth and hoarding it: the passage says the miser's wealth will not help him and describes the giver as giving wealth to purify himself.
rows.anchor: وإنه لكذلك، الإعطاء للمال والبخل به، في آيتي الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving or withholding wealth concerns what should be spent for good and God's due to its rightful recipients through alms, charity, and generosity.
rows.anchor: فيما يجب أن ينفق فيه المال من وجوه الخير، وأداء حق الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas interprets he was mindful as he avoided stinginess.
rows.anchor: قول عن ابن عباس أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Ibn Abbas's reading because giving already contrasts with stinginess and the later contrast opposes giving and mindfulness to stinginess and denial.
rows.anchor: مما يبعد أن يكون اتقى بمعنى اتقى البخل

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The two other reported objects of mindfulness are God or the reckoning and punishment; the author regards them as closely related.
rows.anchor: والوجهان متقاربان، فمن اتقى الله عذابه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa originally means protection from harm; Quranic usage associates it with avoiding sin to seek God's approval and protection from His anger and punishment.
rows.anchor: والوقاية في الأصل الحفظ مما يضر ويؤذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Quranic usage, the object of taqwa is often omitted with past or present verbs, but when stated it is God; the overall usage supports fearing God, His reckoning, and His punishment.
rows.anchor: وهذا الاستقراء يؤذن بأن الاتقاء في القرآن يغلب أن يكون اتقاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa is an inward act of the heart, as shown by verses that locate it in the heart and say God receives people's piety rather than sacrificial flesh and blood.
rows.anchor: من أفعال القلوب. بمعنى أنها لا تكون إلا في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran contrasts taqwa with wickedness and corruption.
rows.anchor: وجاءت التقوى نقيضاً للفجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truthfulness can describe words, deeds, intention, and belief; Quranic affirmation most often means believing in God, His signs, messengers, words, and meeting Him.
rows.anchor: وأكثر ما يكون التصديق في القرآن الكريم بمعناه الديني في التصديق بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author keeps al-husna broad enough to include the interpretations of reward in this life and the next, Paradise, recompense, and monotheism.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الأولى إطلاقها لتعم فلا تختص بوجه من هذه الوجوه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Exegetes explain making the way easy as preparing the state most convenient for the one who affirms the good, in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: وفسروا الآية بأنها التهيئة للحالة التي هي أيسر على المصدق بالحسنى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the paths are called easy and hard for their outcomes, or they mean the routes to Paradise and Hell.
rows.anchor: سمى طريقة الخير باليسرى لأن عاقبتها اليسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise to make the easy way accessible appears with yusra only in al-Ala 87:8 and here, for the Prophet and for the giver who is mindful and affirms the good.
rows.anchor: التيسير لليسرى هو وعد الله للباذلين المعطين المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Usra appears in this form only in al-Layl; Quranic uses of usr and its derivatives connect hardship to the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: أما العسرى فلم تأت بهذه الصيغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the claim that al-usra was chosen just to preserve the rhyme, and reports al-Zamakhshari's account of God's withholding help as a Mu'tazilite insinuation noted by Abu Hayyan.
rows.anchor: فما يجوز في البيان العالي التعلق بملحظ شكل في اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the verbal nouns usr and yusr, usra and yusra convey the extreme of hardship or ease, as do Quranic forms such as the greatest seizure and the greatest Fire.
rows.anchor: وإنما الملحوظ فيهما، بصيغة الفعلى، أقصى اليسر وأشد العسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the most difficult way easy is emphatic warning, comparable to the Quran's ironic announcement of painful punishment for hoarders and other opponents.
rows.anchor: كالتيسير للعسرى: مبالغة في الردع والنذير لمن بخل واستغنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghina can mean self-sufficiency even without wealth, while thara denotes possession of wealth unless used figuratively.
rows.anchor: الفرق بين الغنى والثراء، إذ يغلب أن يكون الغنى غنى النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rada originally means destruction and includes the physical image of a rock or falling into a well, then extends to ruin generally.
rows.anchor: وتردى في البئر سقط، ثم استعمل في مطلق الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taradda is the intransitive form of arda, to destroy or cause ruin; the Quran uses the root in related forms for perishing, causing ruin, and a fallen animal, and this exhausts its occurrences.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو كل ما في القرآن من المادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author understands taradda as plunging into ruin and prefers al-Tabari's reading as falling into Hell over the reported burial-shroud reading.
rows.anchor: أقرب إلى المعنى والسياق من قول قوم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan transmits the alternative reading of taradda as being covered by a burial shroud, supported by lines from Malik ibn al-Rayb and another poet.
rows.anchor: من قول قوم، فيما نقل أبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shroud reading does not fit the warning against the miser, since death in a shroud applies to believers as well as disbelievers.
rows.anchor: لأن التردى برداء الكفن لا يختص به كافر دون مؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda means guidance to the straight path and usually contrasts with misguidance and disbelief; al-akhira and al-ula mean end and beginning, and in religious usage the afterlife and this world.
rows.anchor: الهدى الإرشاد إلى الطريق المستقيم، وأكثر ما يجيء في القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says God owns both worlds and gives or withholds as He wills, guiding some to obedience and honor and abandoning others to disobedience and punishment.
rows.anchor: لنا ملك ما في الدنيا والآخرة، نعطى منهما من أردنا من خلقنا ونحرم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari and Abu Hayyan restrict the promise to reward in both abodes for those who are guided.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري في (الكشاف) على ثواب الدارين للمهتدى

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi reports that God owns everything in both worlds, so accepting or refusing guidance benefits or harms people, not God; had He willed, He could have prevented their disobedience.
rows.anchor: إن لنا كل ما في الدنيا والآخرة فليس يضرنا ترككم الاهتداء بهدانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the negative parsing of ma because it emphatically states that wealth cannot help the miser when he falls into ruin.
rows.anchor: والنفي عندنا أولى، لما فيه من ملحظ التقرير لعدم غنى المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning of blazing Fire is general, like the statement that human efforts diverge; the next verse specifies that the most wretched person who denies and turns away enters it.
rows.anchor: والإنذار بنار تلظى، في آية الليل، عام كالعموم المستفاد من الآية قبله

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Some interpret la yaslaha as meaning that only the most wretched warms himself by the Fire.
rows.anchor: لا يصطلي بها إلا الأشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects that gloss: saly means putting something into fire or enduring its heat, while istisla is usually seeking warmth from fire.
rows.anchor: أما الاصطلاء فقلما يستعمل إلا في التماس الدفء من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran reserves istisla for warmth, as in Moses' words at the fire, but uses saly for punishment and enduring the heat of Hell, consistently naming disbelievers and the deluded by wealth, status, or children.
rows.anchor: ويختص الصلى فيها جميعاً، فعلاً ومصدراً واسم فاعل، بنار الجحيم
